advances: Global evenness cannot be deleted from the fixed-original-fiber actual-depth conclusion of accepted fact 790af4eef0a586aa, even if the complete central residual lattice table is invariant under both coordinate sign changes and has mean zero. The counterexamples below are explicit rational convex bodies whose complete actual volume tables have first-block mean exactly zero in every finite dimension used. One vertical halfspace bounds the depth of every point in the prescribed integer fiber by a quantity that is negligible compared with \(W/2^3\). An explicit point in another integer fiber has depth at least \(W/10\), so these bodies do not disprove the locked weak Oertel conjecture.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Accepted fact 790af4eef0a586aa supplies the precise hypothesis list, notation, and fixed-original-fiber conclusion being tested. No depth conclusion from that fact is applied to the noneven potential. The body construction, exact complete volumes, convexity and global extension, moment identities, numerical bounds, and both halfspace-depth assertions are proved directly above.
proof:
The set \(Q_m\) is a compact convex box with nonempty interior and is invariant under each coordinate sign change. The integer coordinates of \(P_m\) range exactly over the three sets in the displayed census of \(D_m\). This proves the full census, including all boundary sites. Every vertex of \(P_m\) is integral and belongs to \(D_m\). Hence \(P_m=\operatorname{conv}D_m\), and therefore \(D_m=\operatorname{conv}D_m\cap\mathbb Z^3\). Its first-block projection is \(\{-1,0,1\}\), which lies in \(\{-1\}\cup\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and has convex hull \(R=[-1,1]\). Every second-block site lies in \(Q_m\), and the central slice is precisely \(\{y:(0,y)\in D_m\}=Q_m\cap\mathbb Z^2\). These are exactly the support hypotheses of 790af4eef0a586aa under the stated map.

The function \(\Psi_m\) is the maximum of the seven affine functions consisting of \(0\), the two functions \(\sigma u-2mv\), and the four functions \(\sigma u+8m\tau v-6m\), where \(\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}\). It is globally finite, convex, continuous, and piecewise affine, with rational coefficients. The zero term ensures nonnegativity, and substitution gives \(\Psi_m(0,0)=0\).

For every \((x,u,v)\in P_m\), one has \(|u|\le m\) and \(|v+x/2|\le3/2\). The second term defining \(\Psi_m(u,v+x/2)\) is at most \(m+3m=4m\); its third term is at most \(m+12m-6m=7m\). Thus

\[
0\le\Psi_m(u,v+x/2)\le7m,
\qquad
\frac12\le1-\frac{\Psi_m(u,v+x/2)}{14m}\le1
\quad((x,u,v)\in P_m).
\]

The roof height in this formula is continuous and concave on \(P_m\). Its hypograph constraints, together with the box constraints and \(z_j\ge0\), define a closed convex set. Equivalently, for each of the seven affine functions just listed, the corresponding constraint is \(14m z_j+L(u,v+x/2)\le14m\). All these coefficients and all box endpoints are rational. There are finitely many constraints, and \(C_m\subseteq P_m\times[0,1]^d\), so \(C_m\) is a compact rational convex polytope. It contains the open set \(\operatorname{int}(P_m)\times(0,1/2)^d\), which is nonempty because \(m\ge1\). Thus it is full dimensional in \(\mathbb R^{3+d}\).

At every \(\mathbf I\in D_m\), the defining constraints give exactly the cube with the stated side length, which lies between \(1/2\) and \(1\). At every integer site outside \(D_m\), the projection constraint excludes the entire fiber. Taking the \(d\)-dimensional volume of these cubes proves the complete actual volume formula, before any potential representation is used. The side lengths are rational and the exponent \(d=14m\) is an integer, so these are exact rational volumes. At the origin the side length is one.

The two formulas for \(g_m\) agree at \(7m\), both giving \(14m\log2\). On \(0<t<7m\), its derivative is \(1/(1-t/(14m))\), increasing from \(1\) to \(2\); on \(t>7m\), its derivative is \(2\). The one-sided derivatives agree at the junction. Thus \(g_m\) is finite, nondecreasing, and convex on \([0,\infty)\), and \(g_m(0)=0\). Its nonnegativity follows as well. For any \(a,b\in\mathbb R^2\) and \(0\le\theta\le1\), convexity of \(\Psi_m\), monotonicity of \(g_m\), and convexity of \(g_m\), in that order, give

\[
\begin{aligned}
F_m((1-\theta)a+\theta b)
&\le g_m((1-\theta)\Psi_m(a)+\theta\Psi_m(b))\\
&\le(1-\theta)F_m(a)+\theta F_m(b).
\end{aligned}
\]

This proves global convexity of \(F_m\), and its finiteness, nonnegativity, and value zero at the origin follow from the definitions. At \((0,1/2)\), the three terms defining \(\Psi_m\) are \(0,-m,-2m\); at \((0,-1/2)\), they are \(0,m,-2m\). Hence the two values of \(\Psi_m\) are \(0\) and \(m\), respectively, proving the asserted unequal values of \(F_m\) at opposite points.

The previously proved bound \(\Psi_m(u,v+x/2)\le7m\) means that the logarithmic branch of \(g_m\) is used everywhere on \(P_m\), including its boundary. Consequently

\[
e^{-F_m(u,v+x/2)}
=\exp\left(14m\log\left(1-\frac{\Psi_m(u,v+x/2)}{14m}\right)\right)
=\left(1-\frac{\Psi_m(u,v+x/2)}{14m}\right)^{14m}.
\]

Since \(y-Bx=(u,v+x/2)\) and \(V=0\), this proves the exact additive-shear representation of the complete actual table. It also gives \(\phi_m(\mathbf0)=0\) and \(w^{(m)}_{\mathbf0}=1\). Composing the convex \(F_m\) with the linear shear shows that \(\phi_m\) is convex on \(P_m\). Define \(f_m=e^{-\phi_m}\) on \(P_m\) and \(f_m=0\) elsewhere. If both endpoints lie in \(P_m\), convexity of \(P_m\) and \(\phi_m\) gives the log-concavity inequality for \(f_m\). If either endpoint lies outside \(P_m\) and \(0<\theta<1\), the right-hand side of that inequality is zero, so nonnegativity proves it. The endpoint cases \(\theta=0,1\) hold directly. This proves the claimed global extension, including all table zeros.

We now evaluate every row of every original integer layer. For \(|u|\le m\), direct substitution into the three defining terms gives

\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
t&-3/2&-1&-1/2&0&1/2&1&3/2\\ \hline
\Psi_m(u,t)
&|u|+6m&|u|+2m&|u|+m&|u|&0&|u|+2m&|u|+6m.
\end{array}
\]

At \(t=-1\), the second and third terms both equal \(|u|+2m\). At \(t=-3/2\), the third term \(|u|+6m\) dominates the second term \(|u|+3m\); at \(t=-1/2\), the second term \(|u|+m\) dominates the third term \(|u|-2m\) and zero. At \(t=0\), the second term is \(|u|\) and the third is \(|u|-6m\). At \(t=1/2\), the nonzero terms are \(|u|-m\) and \(|u|-2m\), both nonpositive. At \(t=1\) and \(t=3/2\), the third term gives the displayed value and dominates the other terms. These comparisons remain valid at \(|u|=m\), including the zero tie at \(t=1/2\).

Substituting \(t=v+x/2\) therefore yields the complete nine-row table

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
&v=-1&v=0&v=1\\ \hline
x=-1&|u|+6m&|u|+m&0\\
x=0&|u|+2m&|u|&|u|+2m\\
x=1&|u|+m&0&|u|+6m.
\end{array}
\]

Every entry is the value of \(\Psi_m(u,v+x/2)\), for every integer \(-m\le u\le m\). Raising one minus the entry divided by \(14m\) to the power \(14m\) gives the actual fiber volume. The central row of this table proves the complete central-weight formula in the statement. Its support is invariant under each sign change, and its positive values depend only on \(|u|\) and \(|v|\). A site outside that support remains outside it after either sign change. This proves sign symmetry of the complete central table. Pairing \(u\) with \(-u\), and separately \(v\) with \(-v\), cancels both central weighted coordinates. The central total is positive because it includes the origin weight one, so its normalized mean is zero.

For either \(x=-1\) or \(x=1\), the total actual weight is exactly \(N_m+A_{1,m}+A_{6,m}\). At \(x=0\), it is \(A_{0,m}+2A_{2,m}\). Summation proves the formula for \(W_m\), and equality of the two off-center totals proves the exact first-block moment

\[
\sum_{D_m}xw^{(m)}_{(x,u,v)}
=-(N_m+A_{1,m}+A_{6,m})
+(N_m+A_{1,m}+A_{6,m})=0.
\]

The support and every weight are even in \(u\), so the full \(u\)-moment is also zero. The \(v\)-moment of the \(x=-1\) layer is \(N_m-A_{6,m}\), that of the \(x=0\) layer is zero, and that of the \(x=1\) layer is \(A_{6,m}-A_{1,m}\). Their sum is \(N_m-A_{1,m}\). Each summand in \(A_{1,m}\) is strictly less than one because its cost \(|u|+m\) is positive, so \(A_{1,m}<N_m\). This proves all moment claims directly for the actual volumes at every integer \(m\).

The required uniform numerical bounds follow from elementary inequalities. For \(0\le t\le7m\),

\[
-\log(1-t/(14m))
=\int_0^{t/(14m)}\frac{da}{1-a}
\ge\frac{t}{14m},
\qquad
\left(1-\frac{t}{14m}\right)^{14m}\le e^{-t}.
\]

Applying this to \(t=|u|+jm\), which lies in \([0,7m]\) for all indices used, gives

\[
0<A_{j,m}
\le e^{-jm}\left(1+2\sum_{k=1}^{m}e^{-k}\right)
<e^{-jm}\left(1+\frac{2}{e-1}\right)
<3e^{-jm}.
\]

The finite geometric sum is strictly smaller than the infinite sum, and the final strict inequality follows from \(e>2\), which follows from the positive terms after \(1+1\) in the exponential series. Since \(m\ge1\), these estimates give

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_{0,m}+2A_{1,m}+A_{2,m}+A_{6,m}
&<3+3+\frac34+\frac3{64}
=\frac{435}{64}<7,\\
A_{0,m}+2A_{1,m}+2A_{2,m}+2A_{6,m}
&<3+3+\frac32+\frac3{32}
=\frac{243}{32}<8.
\end{aligned}
\]

Every \(A_{j,m}\) is positive, so the total formula yields \(2N_m<W_m<2N_m+8\). Since \(N_m\ge3\), one has \(8\le3N_m\), proving \(W_m<2N_m+8\le5N_m\).

The halfspace \(H_m^-\) depends only on the original integer coordinates. In the layer \(x=-1\), its inequality allows exactly \(v=-1,0\); in the layer \(x=0\), exactly \(v=-1,0\); and in the layer \(x=1\), exactly \(v=-1\). There is no restriction on \(u\) or the continuous coordinate within any included fiber. The nine-row table therefore gives

\[
\mathcal H_d(S_m\cap H_m^-)
=(A_{6,m}+A_{1,m})+(A_{2,m}+A_{0,m})+A_{1,m}.
\]

This counts the full boundary mass at \(x=0,v=0\). In particular, every point \((\mathbf0,z)\) with \(z\in[0,1]^d\) lies in this closed halfspace. The defining infimum of depth consequently gives the same upper bound for every such \(z\). Using the strict bound by \(7\) and \(W_m>2N_m=4m+2\),

\[
\sup_{z\in(C_m)_{\mathbf0}}
\frac{h_{S_m}((\mathbf0,z))}{W_m/8}
\le\frac{8\,\mathcal H_d(S_m\cap H_m^-)}{W_m}
<\frac{56}{4m+2}.
\]

Depth is nonnegative, so the displayed limit in the statement follows. The fixed-origin-fiber conclusion of 790af4eef0a586aa would require this supremum to be at least \(1/528\). At \(m=7392\), one has \(4m+2=29570>56\cdot528=29568\), giving the explicit failure. More generally, the limit excludes every positive constant in that prescribed-fiber conclusion when global evenness is removed.

It remains to check a point with uniformly large depth in the same actual bodies. At every site \((1,u,0)\) with \(-m\le u\le m\), the nine-row table has cost zero. Therefore the measurable subset

\[
T_m=\{(1,u,0,z):u\in\{-m,-m+1,\ldots,m\},\ z\in[0,1]^d\}
\]

is contained in \(S_m\), has mixed volume \(N_m\), and contains \(\mathbf p_m^+\). Reflection about \(\mathbf p_m^+\) sends each of its points to \((1,-u,0,\mathbf1_d-z)\). It maps \(T_m\) bijectively to itself and preserves its mixed volume: it permutes the integer fibers and preserves Lebesgue measure in each continuous cube.

Take any closed ambient halfspace \(H=\{q:\ell(q)\le b\}\) containing \(\mathbf p_m^+\), where \(\ell\) is linear, so \(b\ge\ell(\mathbf p_m^+)\). Write \(\rho(q)=2\mathbf p_m^+-q\). If both \(q\) and \(\rho(q)\) were outside \(H\), then
\(\ell(q)+\ell(\rho(q))>2b\ge2\ell(\mathbf p_m^+)\), contrary to the equality \(\ell(q)+\ell(\rho(q))=2\ell(\mathbf p_m^+)\). Thus \(T_m\subseteq H\cup\rho(H)\). Reflection invariance of \(T_m\) and its measure gives

\[
N_m
\le\mathcal H_d(T_m\cap H)+\mathcal H_d(T_m\cap\rho(H))
=2\mathcal H_d(T_m\cap H)
\le2\mathcal H_d(S_m\cap H).
\]

This argument uses weak halfspace membership and remains valid when the boundary carries positive mixed volume. It holds for every containing closed halfspace, with the same point \(\mathbf p_m^+\) chosen in advance. Taking the infimum proves \(h_{S_m}(\mathbf p_m^+)\ge N_m/2\ge W_m/10\). Since \(e>2\), every \(c_0\in(0,1/e)\) satisfies \(c_0/2^3<1/16<1/10\), so this point satisfies the locked conjecture's bound for every allowed \(c_0\) on these bodies. The failure proved above is confined to the prescribed original integer fiber.
statement:
For every integer \(m\ge1\), set \(r=1\), \(s=2\), \(n=3\), and \(d=14m\). Write the integer coordinates as \(\mathbf I=(x,y)=(x,u,v)\), where \(y=(u,v)\), and use \(z\in\mathbb R^d\) for the continuous coordinates. The integer target is \(\mathbf0=(0,0,0)\). Define

\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_m&=[-m,m]\times[-1,1],
&P_m&=[-1,1]\times Q_m,
&D_m&=P_m\cap\mathbb Z^3,\\
R&=[-1,1],
&V(x)&=0\quad(x\in R),
&B&=(0,-1/2)^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus \(y-Bx=(u,v+x/2)\). Define the auxiliary convex function and the residual potential by

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Psi_m(u,v)&=\max\{0,\ |u|-2mv,\ |u|+8m|v|-6m\},\\
g_m(t)&=
\begin{cases}
-14m\log(1-t/(14m)),&0\le t\le7m,\\
14m\log2+2(t-7m),&t>7m,
\end{cases}\\
F_m(u,v)&=g_m(\Psi_m(u,v)),\\
\phi_m(x,y)&=V(x)+F_m(y-Bx).
\end{aligned}
\]

All logarithms are natural. The function \(F_m:\mathbb R^2\to[0,\infty)\) is globally finite and convex, and \(F_m(0,0)=0\), but it is not even: \(F_m(0,1/2)=0\) and \(F_m(0,-1/2)=-14m\log(13/14)>0\).

Let

\[
C_m=\left\{(x,u,v,z)\in\mathbb R^{3+d}:
(x,u,v)\in P_m,\quad
0\le z_j\le1-\frac{\Psi_m(u,v+x/2)}{14m}
\quad(1\le j\le d)\right\}.
\]

This is a full-dimensional compact rational convex polytope. Write \((C_m)_{\mathbf I}=\{z:(\mathbf I,z)\in C_m\}\), \(\Lambda_m=\mathbb Z^3\times\mathbb R^d\), and \(S_m=C_m\cap\Lambda_m\). Its complete integer-fiber volume table is exactly

\[
w^{(m)}_{\mathbf I}
:=\mathcal L^d((C_m)_{\mathbf I})
=
\begin{cases}
\left(1-\dfrac{\Psi_m(u,v+x/2)}{14m}\right)^{14m}
=e^{-\phi_m(x,u,v)},&\mathbf I=(x,u,v)\in D_m,\\
0,&\mathbf I\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus D_m.
\end{cases}
\]

Every fiber at a site of \(D_m\) is a positive-volume cube, every other integer fiber is empty, and \((C_m)_{\mathbf0}=[0,1]^d\). Put \(W_m=\mathcal H_d(S_m)=\sum_{\mathbf I\in D_m}w^{(m)}_{\mathbf I}>0\).

The notation map to accepted fact 790af4eef0a586aa is \(Q=Q_m\), \(P=P_m\), \(D=D_m\), \(F=F_m\), \(\phi=\phi_m\), \(w=w^{(m)}\), \(W=W_m\), \(C=C_m\), and \(S=S_m\); its \(r,s,n,d,R,V,B\) have the meanings just specified. Its proportionality constant is \(\alpha=1\), so its scalar table and its complete actual table agree exactly, with \(W_C=W_m\). These objects satisfy every support, convexity, normalization, and first-block-stationarity hypothesis in that fact except for global evenness of \(F\). In addition, \(e^{-\phi_m}\) on \(P_m\), extended by zero off \(P_m\), is a finite-valued nonnegative log-concave extension of the complete table to \(\mathbb R^3\).

More explicitly, the complete positive support is

\[
D_m=\{-1,0,1\}\times\{-m,-m+1,\ldots,m\}\times\{-1,0,1\},
\qquad |D_m|=9(2m+1).
\]

At first block zero, the central table is

\[
w^{(m)}_{(0,u,v)}
=
\begin{cases}
\left(1-\dfrac{|u|+2m|v|}{14m}\right)^{14m},
&(u,v)\in Q_m\cap\mathbb Z^2,\\
0,&(u,v)\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus Q_m.
\end{cases}
\]

For every \((u,v)\in\mathbb Z^2\) and \(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in\{-1,1\}\), one has \(w^{(m)}_{(0,\epsilon_1u,\epsilon_2v)}=w^{(m)}_{(0,u,v)}\), including every zero entry. This central residual table has normalized mean \((0,0)\).

For the following exact totals, set \(N_m=2m+1\) and

\[
A_{j,m}=\sum_{u=-m}^{m}
\left(1-\frac{|u|+jm}{14m}\right)^{14m}
\qquad(j\in\{0,1,2,6\}).
\]

Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
W_m&=2N_m+A_{0,m}+2A_{1,m}+2A_{2,m}+2A_{6,m},\\
\sum_{(x,u,v)\in D_m}xw^{(m)}_{(x,u,v)}&=0,
&\sum_{(x,u,v)\in D_m}uw^{(m)}_{(x,u,v)}&=0,\\
\sum_{(x,u,v)\in D_m}vw^{(m)}_{(x,u,v)}
&=N_m-A_{1,m}>0,
&2N_m<W_m&<2N_m+8\le5N_m.
\end{aligned}
\]

In particular, the actual first-block mean is exactly zero, while the full integer-marginal mean is \((0,0,(N_m-A_{1,m})/W_m)\ne\mathbf0\).

For \(\mathbf p\in S_m\), let \(h_{S_m}(\mathbf p)\) be the infimum of \(\mathcal H_d(S_m\cap H)\) over all closed ambient halfspaces \(H\) containing \(\mathbf p\), as in the locked problem. The fixed vertical halfspace
\(H_m^-=\{(x,u,v,z)\in\mathbb R^{3+d}:x+2v\le0\}\) contains the entire prescribed fiber \(\{\mathbf0\}\times[0,1]^d\) and satisfies

\[
\mathcal H_d(S_m\cap H_m^-)
=A_{0,m}+2A_{1,m}+A_{2,m}+A_{6,m}<7.
\]

Consequently,

\[
0\le
\sup_{z\in(C_m)_{\mathbf0}}
\frac{h_{S_m}((\mathbf0,z))}{W_m/2^3}
<\frac{56}{4m+2}
\longrightarrow0
\qquad(m\longrightarrow\infty).
\]

For example, \(m=7392\) already makes this supremum strictly smaller than \(1/528\), so no point in that prescribed fiber satisfies the lower bound in the conditional actual-body conclusion of 790af4eef0a586aa after global evenness is deleted. Nevertheless, with \(\mathbf J_+=(1,0,0)\) and \(\mathbf p_m^+=(\mathbf J_+,\tfrac12\mathbf1_d)\), one has

\[
\mathbf p_m^+\in S_m,
\qquad
h_{S_m}(\mathbf p_m^+)\ge\frac{N_m}{2}\ge\frac{W_m}{10}.
\]
